correctness.rationale: On the open support put δ=p+1−x>0 and K=p/(p+1)^p>0. The density is Kδ^(p−1), its derivative is −(p−1)Kδ^(p−2), and the second derivative of its logarithm is −(p−1)/δ². Therefore it strictly increases to infinity for 0<p<1, is the constant 1/2 for p=1, and strictly decreases to zero for p>1; in the last case the left limit p/(p+1) is the supremum, not an attained maximum on the open interval. The ordinary second derivative has constant sign as well, since f''/f=(p−1)(p−2)/δ². The survival integral is (δ/(p+1))^p, giving exactly the stated hazard p/δ and its positive derivative p/δ². The publisher's PDF directly states the incompatible Figure 1 prose (including right-endpoint blow-up in all cases), and §2.3 calls the density decreasing for 0<p≤1 immediately after giving the log derivative that shows otherwise. This check concerns the published interpretation; no assertion about the rendered curve strokes is needed. The supplied checker was inspected but not executed; representative numerical cases are unnecessary for the all-parameter analytic proof.

value.rationale: This is worthwhile as a narrow published correction, not as a textbook differentiation exercise. It replaces an erroneous common-shape and blow-up description with the correct parameter-dependent behavior, distinguishes a boundary supremum from a mode in the open support, and preserves the separate increasing-hazard conclusion. The correction changes how users of the proposed model interpret density near the upper bound.
